recipes.name: Cake Mix Cinnamon Rolls
ingredients_raw: 0.25 cup chopped pecans, or to taste

steps.text: Pour warm water into a bowl; add yeast and let stand until creamy, about 10 minutes.

Combine yeast mixture, cake mix, and 3 cups of flour in a large bowl; stir well. Add remaining flour, 1/2 cup at a time, stirring well after each addition until dough pulls together. Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic, about 8 minutes.
Lightly oil a large bowl; place dough in the bowl and turn to coat with oil. Cover with a damp cloth and let rise in a warm place until doubled in volume, about 30 minutes.

Deflate dough and turn it out onto a lightly floured surface. Roll the dough into a 10x16-inch rectangle. Spread softened butter over the rectangle; sprinkle on brown sugar and cinnamon. Starting from one of the long sides, roll up the rectangle and cut into 1-inch wide rolls.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease a 9x13-inch baking pan.

Pour melted butter into a small bowl. Mix the white sugar and pecans in another small bowl. Dip the top of each roll in melted butter, then in sugar and pecan mixture, then arrange rolls snugly in the prepared pan. Cover rolls with a damp cloth and let rise until doubled in volume, about 30 minutes.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Cake Mix Cinnamon Rolls
raw_recipe.description: These cake mix cinnamon rolls combine yeast with boxed white cake mix for soft, scrumptious cinnamon rolls. Try this recipe with different cake mixes.

video.description: These cinnamon rolls are made with a box of cake mix! This easy recipe is great to prep the night before and bake in the morning for breakfast or brunch!
video.name: How to Make Cake Mix Cinnamon Rolls

review.reviewBody: Thank you Arvilla for sharing this wonderful recipe. The only change I made was that I used Spice cake mix instead of white. I made them and shared them with all my neighbors and they raved about them. Thanks again! Do yourself a favor and try these. They are GREAT!

I made this Christmas morning w/ a butter pecan cake mix-everyone LOVED it and it was to die for!! They were so soft and gooey! My first time making bread of any kind, it was a very ready recipe!! It made 16 rolls. I let it rise covered in the fridge overnight, and make cream cheese frosting for the top. (1 pkg cream cheese softened, 1 cup powdered sugar, 1/2 tsp vanilla, 6 tbs butter softened) make sure not to over bake.

These were excellent. I was afraid they would be too cake like or too sweet but they weren’t. Next time I will put them in two pans - maybe a 9X 13 and an 8 X 8 because they did not cook evenly when crammed into just the one pan. I had to remove the edge ones (by that I mean eat them haha) and put the rest back in the oven for another 15 minutes. I think giving them more room will help with that. I used my kitchen aid mixer to knead the dough and probably used closer to 5 c flour. I dipped the cut rolls into melted butter then placed them in a pan that was sprinkled with 1/3 c brown sugar and pecans. I drizzled a little extra melted butter on top. Highly recommend and will make again!

I have had this recipe in my to do list for over 5 years. First time using yeast. A lot of work but they came out great. I used a cream cheese frosting on top once they were cool. I had 2 extra rolls for my pan and baked them on cookie sheet for 17 minutes. Family devoured them.

Excellent! I added chopped apples inside. I also added coconut on top with the nuts and sugar. I also put butter, brown sugar and chopped apples on the bottom of the pan for turning the rolls out onto a platter. I drizzled powdered sugar icing on top for added moisture. Definitely flour your hands before handling the sticky dough. I used my Ninja dough setting for bringing the dough together. Then kneaded with floured hands. Pretty easy overall. These rolls could pass as a signature product for a small business as the dough is unique between bread and cake and absolutely endulg-ably delicious and sweet.

These are the BEST!! So quick and easy to make!! I do mine with Rapid Rise Instant Yeast (mix with my dry ingredients), add the warm water, stir with the end of a wooden spatula, knead and let rise in greased bowl, covered (in oven with light on), after it rises (I sometimes do two rises) I roll it out spread the butter, sprinkle on the cinnamon and brown sugar, roll up and cut. I also use gluten free flour and cake mix (makes the fluffiest deliciousness!) Love this recipe and love the reaction I get when people try it. The only bad thing, I've already made it 2 times in one week!! haha But really, thank you for this!! It's the best.

I used a 1 1/2 cups of the brown sugar center and chopped some pecans into the mix with the cinnamon. Somehow I'm not seeing an icing recipe or ingredients so made a basic powdered sugar, butter (creamed) and milk basic icing. The dough was really sticky so just stay with 8 minutes of kneading. Also the directions call for pecans but did not see it listing in the ingredients when I made my batch.

I will make this again and try as other suggested using a spice cake recipe. Will also knead less, rather than keep adding flour to help make it smooth and less sticky. Will also add another teaspoon of cinnamon.

I used this recipe to make plain cinnamon rolls. I have made these rolls three times in the past month. 4-1/2 cups of flour was not near enough to make this dough come together for me. All three times I had a wet soggy doughy mess that was not manageable. I had to add two more cups of flour before being able to work the dough. Not sure why, but the rolls came out beautifully and each batch was well received. I was able to fill two 9x13 pans with twelve rolls each - and the softness of the rolls was outstanding. I do use SAF instant yeast and a pkg of yeast is 7 grams . .so, 21 grams of yeast is aLOT of yeast. This last batch I used a half a cup of butters and cup of brown sugar with two tablespoons of cinnamon. I read all the positive comments and am not sure why only I had an issue with the flour, but the end result was good and leftovers warmed up beautifully in the microwave.

This is a fabulous recipe! All I added to the batter was some grated orange peel for added flavour. I used a french vanilla cake mix and next time I'll try spice or lemon for variation. All the mixing and kneading was done in my KitchenAid - so easy. I used a 9x11 and a 9x9 pan and iced them with cream cheese icing flavoured with more grated orange peel. They are delicious! I will use this recipe again and again. Thank you!

Love this recipe. Instead of cinnamon I spread raspberry jam and add frozen raspberries and let them sit overnight in the fridge. I have also used peach jam and canned peaches. The fruit filling is amazing with these rolls.

halved the recipe, and only used 2 tbs butter to spread on the dough, but much much more cinnamon. i used a milk chocolate cake mix, and let the bread machine mix, knead and rose the dough. easy peasy.
It was a great recipe and very easy to follow.
Followed directions to the letter. Texture & overall look was good, but the flavor didn’t hit. Sticking to traditional cinnamon rolls from here on out.

Very good. I'm not a baker by any means but they came out pretty good. Center was a little undercooked, I baked them for a little over 20 minutes. I'll try longer next time. Easy but time consuming. I'll also probably try to put them together the night before next time so we aren't eating them for lunch.
I made it according to directions and it was too wet I could not get it to form a ball I even used more flour will not be doing this recipe again

Very tasty, good texture, but would definitely use a larger pan next time, and maybe cut rolls smaller. The rolls around the outside were as big as softballs, difficult time getting the middle ones baked--probably twenty extra minutes altogether. Still delicious, tho!

Because I had never tried it, I used rapid rise yeast. I left out the sugar in the dough. When the rolls were still quite warm, I iced them with the most delicious icing. I don’t remember the name, but it starts with butter and cream cheese! They were great! A keeper!
